 The Boston Celtics have experienced a little bit of everything in the opening week of the 2026-27 NBA season.
 After blowing a 22-point lead in a season-opening loss to the Detroit Pistons, the Celtics have responded with three straight wins, capped by Jayson Tatum's overtime buzzer-beater against the Brooklyn Nets.
 The Celtics are still figuring out their new-look roster, but their first four games have revealed some encouraging signs and some areas of concern.
 Here are four things we've learned about the Celtics so far.
 MORE:  Jaylen Brown Has Blunt Response to Brian Scalabrine's Celtics Trade Claim 
 4 Things We've Learned About the Celtics After 4 Games
 1. Jayson Tatum looks like Jayson Tatum again
 Tatum's season didn't get off to an ideal start, but he's looked much more like himself since his clunker against the Pistons.
 Over his last three games, Tatum is averaging 33.0 points, 7.0 rebounds, 7.0 assists and 1.3 steals while shooting 49.2 percent from the field. He capped off that stretch with a 40-point performance against the Nets, his best game since returning from his Achilles injury.
 HAVE YOURSELF A NIGHT, JAYSON TATUM! ☘️ 40 PTS ☘️ 8 AST ☘️ 5 REB ☘️ 1 @TISSOT BUZZER-BEATER IN OT Tonight marks his 7th career game-winning shot with under 3 seconds remaining... that's the most since the start of the 2019-20 NBA season! https://t.co/I0du5uQhvS
— NBA (@NBA) October 28, 2026 Tatum's improved efficiency is particularly encouraging after he shot just 41.1 percent from the field in 16 regular-season games following his return last season.
 Tatum isn't just scoring at a high level, either. He also leads the Celtics with 32 assists and just seven turnovers through four games, making for  one of the best playmaking stretches of his career .
 The Celtics should be in good shape if Tatum can sustain that combination of scoring and playmaking.
 2. Paul George fits like a glove
 On both ends of the court.
 Offensively, George has been good for 22.3 points per game on a scorching 43.8 percent from 3-point range. Defensively, he's using his length and anticipation to make plays, ranking among the league leaders in both steals and deflections.
 George has also shown off his defensive versatility. We've already seen him guard a bruising forward in Julius Randle, a shifty guard in Cade Cunningham and an athletic wing in Caleb Wilson.
 Paul George, the defensive menace https://t.co/LdxW63Zs8F
— Tomek Kordylewski (@Timi_093) October 24, 2026 He's not Jaylen Brown, but a healthy George gives the Celtics another proven two-way option alongside Tatum.
 MORE:  Everyone Is Talking About The Same Jayson Tatum Stat After His Buzzer-Beater 
 3. Derrick White's 3-point shooting is off to a worrying start
 The hope was that Tatum's return and George's arrival would ease some of White's offensive burden and help him rediscover his shooting touch.
 That hasn't been the case.
 White is 7-for-22 (31.8 percent) from 3-point range to start the season. More concerning, 19 of White's 22 attempts have come when he was open or wide open, according to NBA.com , meaning the nearest defender was at least four feet away.
 In other words, White is missing a lot of good looks.
 It's still too early to panic, but with how much he struggled from the perimeter last season, it's certainly one to watch.
 4. Paint scoring is still a problem
 After Boston's loss to Philadelphia in the playoffs last season, Celtics president Brad Stevens talked about the need to have more of an impact at the rim.
 How's that going? Well, the Celtics are averaging  42.5  points in the paint through four games this season, down from  44.3  per game last season.
 It's a small sample, of course, but it's not a huge surprise given that Brown was one of the NBA's leading paint scorers last season, while George is more of a shooter. Tatum can help fill some of that void, but the Celtics will need contributions from the rest of the roster to become a more balanced offensive team.
 An encouraging sign: Boston scored a season-high 52 points in the paint  against Brooklyn, helping it win despite shooting 11-for-41 from 3.
 That's the type of production that could help the Celtics become a more balanced offensive team.
